note.p: It is likely that all the later entries of Arch in London, and potentially the earlier entry in Ireland, referred to the booksellers John and Arthur Arch. John and Arthur Arch were partners in the bookselling business, from 1792-1838. They resided in Gracechurch St initially but from 1805 onwards, their address was 61 Cornhill. They were Quakers, publishing a large portion of Quaker texts, art from the Royal Academy, and other publishments. Notably, in 1798, they published Blank Verse by Charles Lamb and Charles Lloyd and were dedicated in the version seen in the Internet Archive. An Arch is frequently seen to be with Charles Lamb, which is why it likely to be one of, or both, John and Arthur Arch. John Arch’s will was dated 1815 and referred to him as the publisher of London Price Current in Bethnal Green, however there was also a will in 1853 of a John Arch. Arthur Portsmouth Arch’s will of 1839 referred to him as a gentleman of Winterslow Place North Brixton.
